data.name: Imperium of the Stars
data.detailed_description:
Imperium of the Stars is a real-time 4X grand strategy where each faction is a different game. Not different bonuses. Different economies, different research, different reasons to exist.

Rule a Gothic empire of cathedral worlds where faith runs like infrastructure. Unmake the galaxy world by world and call it healing. Or forge a warhost from salvage and prove your Pack-Lord in blood.

Then there is the Lattice. Crystalline, with no history here before the Long Silence.

Three hundred years after the warp went quiet, the galaxy is still deciding what it becomes. Up to 10,000 procedurally generated star systems. No diplomacy. Only war.

  • 1,000 to 10,000 star systems, with configurable shape and compaction

  • Four asymmetric factions, Separate mechanics, separate tech trees, different power structure and different abilities and actions you can do, every faction almost plays like a different game

  • No diplomacy between the great powers. The war is permanent, and everyone plays by their own rules

  • Faith and loyalty are resources. Loyalty is kept by faith, and loyalty improves what worlds bring in

  • Orders go out empire-wide, Macro management is the core of the game, not an afterthought

  • A Game Director you can retune mid-campaign, from Balanced to Grimdark. Dynamic difficulty an answer to snowballing, so winning early does not turn the rest into a formality

The Factions

The Imperium seeks to reunite a shattered galaxy and calls it salvation. The Void Eternal seeks to return creation to the silence that came before it, and calls that peace. The Grokhar take what they can hold.

They are permanently at war, and what changes hands are the remnant systems. You steer where your faction goes, so no two runs go the same way.

Each has its own mechanics and its own tech tree, asymmetric enough that playing another feels close to playing another game.

Events that arrive without asking

A Cardinal petitions for a world you had other plans for. A Void whisper takes hold on a frontier system. A Pack-Lord has gone too long without blood. Some resolve in a single decision, others escalate for months.

Fought in real time

Fleet actions across dozens of ship classes. Ground sieges fought by regiments, where terrain and morale decide as much as numbers.

An empire that runs without you

Declare a sector as an operation, called a Grand Campaign. You set the commitment, the risk and the conditions that end it, and it musters its own task forces (groups of fleets) and runs them. When it cannot advance it says why: no route, outmatched, out of money. A sector governor does the same for building, working from that sector's own resources, and never overrides an order you gave by hand.

None of it is compulsory. You can always drop down and run a single world or a single fleet by hand.

A galaxy that never stands still

The Ordinator is your Game Director. It sets how hard the galaxy pushes back, on presets from Balanced to Grimdark, and you can change it mid-campaign.

Ten thousand worlds. One throne. The void is patient.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS: Windows 10 (64-bit)
  • Processor: Quad-core, 2.5 GHz (e.g. Intel Core i5-7400 / AMD Ryzen 3 1200)
  • Memory: 8 GB RAM
  • Graphics: DirectX 11 (Intel HD 620, AMD Vega 8) 1 GB VRAM
  • DirectX: Version 11
  • Storage: 2 GB available space
  • Additional Notes: Small–medium galaxies. Reduce galaxy size on 8 GB systems.

mac_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS: macOS 11 Big Sur
  • Processor: Apple M3
  • Memory: 8 GB RAM
